newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia banks told to cap base rates - sources.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia banks told to cap base rates - sources.

text.p: Malaysian banks have been asked by the central Bank Negara Malaysia to hold steady their base lending rates (BLR) at 9.67 percent despite the recent spike up in interbank rates, banking sources said on Friday.
A banking source said a circular on the matter was distributed to banks on Thursday.
"A circular has been sent to the banks stating that the BLR ceiling in July is the same as June," said another banking source.
The BLR ceiling in June was fixed at 9.67 percent.
With the exception of Malayan Banking, banks are now quoting base lending rates at between 9.50 and 9.65 percent.
Malayan Banking, Malaysia's largest bank, last month raised its rate to 9.35 percent from 9.10 percent.

Under a new formula announced in October 1995, calculation of BLR is pegged to the average three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) over a month. Bank Negara then fixed a ceiling rate for BLR.
The BLR -- the interest rate banks offer to their best clients for loans -- is a key rate used as a benchmark for other commercial rates.
Analysts had earlier said that the recent surge in interbank rates would lead to another round of increase in base lending rates this month.

Interbank rates rose sharply in recent weeks, triggered by a sudden tightening of liquidity in the system as a result of central Bank Negara's massive intervention in the foreign exchange market to defend the ringgit from a speculative attack.
